claim: Cst7 (encoding cystatin F) is among the most highly upregulated genes in disease-associated microglia in Alzheimer's disease models.
source: Cst7 (encoding cystatin F) is among the most highly upregulated genes in these microglia.
evidence: The manuscript presents RNASeq data showing Cst7 upregulation in multiple AD models, and Figure 1A shows compiled data from six published studies demonstrating dramatic upregulation of Cst7 in microglia across amyloid-driven disease models.

claim: The emergence of disease-associated microglia is emphasized in females compared to males.
source: Transcriptomic studies show that a microglial state characterised by a set of genes involved in endolysosomal function is induced in both mouse Alzheimer's disease (AD) models and human AD brain, and that the emergence of this state is emphasised in females.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, and it is supported by references to published transcriptomic studies and data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing higher expression of DAM/ARM genes in females.

claim: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had greater endolysosomal gene expression compared to Cst7+/+ controls.
source: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had greater endolysosomal gene expression, lysosomal burden, and amyloid beta (Aβ) burden in vivo and were more phagocytic in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by RNASeq data in Figure 2E showing upregulation of endolysosomal genes in female Cst7-/- microglia, with GO enrichment analysis in Figure 2F confirming enrichment of endolysosomal pathways.

claim: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had increased lysosomal burden in vivo.
source: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had greater endolysosomal gene expression, lysosomal burden, and amyloid beta (Aβ) burden in vivo and were more phagocytic in vitro.
evidence: Figure 3H shows increased LAMP2 staining (normalized to IBA1) in the subiculum of female Cst7-/- mice compared to controls, indicating increased lysosomal burden.

claim: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had increased amyloid beta burden in vivo.
source: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had greater endolysosomal gene expression, lysosomal burden, and amyloid beta (Aβ) burden in vivo and were more phagocytic in vitro.
evidence: Figure 4B and 4C show increased percentage of MeX04+ microglia and increased MeX04 median fluorescence intensity in female Cst7-/- mice, indicating greater microglial Aβ burden.

claim: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia were more phagocytic in vitro.
source: In females, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had greater endolysosomal gene expression, lysosomal burden, and amyloid beta (Aβ) burden in vivo and were more phagocytic in vitro.
evidence: Figure 5F and 5G show that female Cst7-/- microglia isolated from AppNL-G-F mice had significantly increased phagocytosis of pHrodo-tagged myelin debris compared to controls.

claim: In males, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia were less inflammatory compared to Cst7+/+ controls.
source: However, in males, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia were less inflammatory and had a reduction in lysosomal burden but had no change in Aβ burden.
evidence: Figure 2G and 2H show downregulation of inflammatory genes (Il1b, Il1a, Tnf, Cxcl2) and enrichment of inflammatory response pathways in male Cst7-/- microglia.

claim: In males, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had a reduction in lysosomal burden.
source: However, in males, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia were less inflammatory and had a reduction in lysosomal burden but had no change in Aβ burden.
evidence: Figure 3H shows reduced LAMP2 staining (normalized to IBA1) in the subiculum of male Cst7-/- mice compared to controls.

claim: In males, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia had no change in Aβ burden compared to controls.
source: However, in males, Cst7-/-AppNL-G-F microglia were less inflammatory and had a reduction in lysosomal burden but had no change in Aβ burden.
evidence: Figure 4B shows no significant difference in percentage of MeX04+ microglia between male Cst7-/- and control mice.

claim: Cst7 is dramatically upregulated in microglia in amyloid-driven disease models.
source: In all models, Cst7 was dramatically upregulated in microglia in amyloid-driven disease and in models where we were able to compare sexes, Cst7 appeared marginally more highly expressed in female disease brains than in male.
evidence: Figure 1A shows compiled data from six published datasets demonstrating dramatic upregulation of Cst7 expression in microglia across multiple amyloid-driven AD models.

claim: Cst7 expression is marginally higher in female disease brains compared to male disease brains.
source: In all models, Cst7 was dramatically upregulated in microglia in amyloid-driven disease and in models where we were able to compare sexes, Cst7 appeared marginally more highly expressed in female disease brains than in male.
evidence: Figure 1A shows data from APP/PS1 and AppNL-G-F models where Cst7 expression appears slightly higher in females, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A shows Cst7 among genes more expressed in female ARMs.

claim: Cst7 expression is almost exclusively localized to disease-derived microglial clusters.
source: To investigate cell-specific expression of Cst7, we mined sequencing databases and found Cst7 is expressed almost exclusively in disease-derived microglial clusters with some minimal expression in homeostatic microglia and negligible expression in other CNS or immune cell subtypes (Zhang et al., 2014; Van Hove et al., 2019; Zeng et al., 2023; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: The text states this finding with citations to published databases, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-D shows expression data from multiple sequencing databases confirming microglial-specific expression.

claim: Cst7 expression is dramatically upregulated around amyloid plaques in AppNL-G-F brains.
source: We found that Cst7 was dramatically upregulated in disease where expression decorated plaques in AppNL-G-F brains (Figure 1B).
evidence: Figure 1B shows in situ hybridization images demonstrating Cst7 expression decorating plaques in AppNL-G-F brains but not in wild-type brains.

claim: Cst7 expression is significantly enriched around plaques compared to areas distant from plaques.
source: Furthermore, expression was significantly enriched around plaques (Figure 1C and D) and almost exclusively localised to IBA1+ cells surrounding plaques (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: Figure 1D shows quantification demonstrating significantly higher Cst7+ area within 25 µm of plaques compared to areas outside this radius.

claim: Cst7 expression is almost exclusively localized to IBA1+ cells surrounding plaques.
source: Furthermore, expression was significantly enriched around plaques (Figure 1C and D) and almost exclusively localised to IBA1+ cells surrounding plaques (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: Figure 1E shows confocal microscopy images demonstrating co-localization of Cst7 with IBA1 around plaques, and Figure 1F quantifies high percentage overlap of Cst7 with IBA1.

claim: AppNL-G-F knock-in led to upregulation of 2022 genes and downregulation of 1849 genes in male microglia.
source: AppNL-G-F knock-in led to numerous changes in gene transcription with 2022 genes upregulated and 1849 downregulated in males and 2053 upregulated and 1857 downregulated in females (Figure 2B).
evidence: Figure 2B shows bar graph quantifying the number of differentially expressed genes in male and female mice comparing wild-type to AppNL-G-F.

claim: AppNL-G-F knock-in led to upregulation of 2053 genes and downregulation of 1857 genes in female microglia.
source: AppNL-G-F knock-in led to numerous changes in gene transcription with 2022 genes upregulated and 1849 downregulated in males and 2053 upregulated and 1857 downregulated in females (Figure 2B).
evidence: Figure 2B shows bar graph quantifying the number of differentially expressed genes in male and female mice comparing wild-type to AppNL-G-F.

claim: Upregulated genes in AppNL-G-F microglia included DAM/ARM genes such as Clec7a, Spp1, Itgax, and Csf1.
source: As expected, upregulated genes included DAM/ARM genes such as Clec7a, Spp1, Itgax, and Csf1, whilst downregulated genes included microglial 'homeostatic' genes P2ry12, Tmem119, and Gpr34 in both sexes (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: Figure 2C and 2D show volcano plots with these genes annotated as significantly upregulated in AppNL-G-F microglia in both females and males.

claim: Downregulated genes in AppNL-G-F microglia included microglial homeostatic genes P2ry12, Tmem119, and Gpr34.
source: As expected, upregulated genes included DAM/ARM genes such as Clec7a, Spp1, Itgax, and Csf1, whilst downregulated genes included microglial 'homeostatic' genes P2ry12, Tmem119, and Gpr34 in both sexes (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: Figure 2C and 2D show volcano plots with these genes annotated as significantly downregulated in AppNL-G-F microglia in both females and males.

claim: Cst7 was among the top 10 most highly upregulated genes in both male and female AppNL-G-F microglia.
source: Cst7 was among the top 10 most highly upregulated genes in males and females.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the volcano plots in Figure 2C and 2D showing Cst7 as a highly significant and highly upregulated gene.

claim: Cst7 deletion led to upregulation of 15 genes and downregulation of 2 genes (including Cst7) in female AppNL-G-F microglia.
source: In females, Cst7 knockout led to upregulation of 15 genes and downregulation of 2 genes (including Cst7) (Figure 2E).
evidence: Figure 2E shows a volcano plot of differentially expressed genes between female AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia.

claim: Female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia were significantly enriched in GO:BP terms such as 'plasma membrane to endosome transport', 'aggrephagy', and 'phagocytosis'.
source: Enrichment analyses revealed that female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia were significantly enriched in GO:BP (Gene Ontology: biological process) terms such as 'plasma membrane to endosome transport', 'aggrephagy', and 'phagocytosis' against their AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ counterparts (Figure 2F).
evidence: Figure 2F shows GO:BP enrichment analysis results listing these terms as significantly enriched in upregulated genes from female Cst7-/- microglia.

claim: Cst7 deletion led to upregulation of 8 genes and downregulation of 51 genes (including Cst7) in male AppNL-G-F microglia.
source: Surprisingly, we observed that male AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia exhibited markedly different transcriptome compared to AppNL-G-F with upregulation of 8 genes and downregulation of 51 genes (including Cst7) (Figure 2G).
evidence: Figure 2G shows a volcano plot of differentially expressed genes between male AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia.

claim: Downregulated genes in male AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia were dominated by classical proinflammatory mediators such as Il1b, Il1a, Tnf, and Cxcl2.
source: In contrast to females, downregulated genes in males were dominated by classical proinflammatory mediators such as Il1b, Il1a, Tnf, and Cxcl2 and enrichment analyses revealed downregulation of GO:BP terms such as 'cellular response to lipopolysaccharide', inflammatory response', and 'NF-kappaB signaling' (Figure 2H).
evidence: Figure 2G shows these genes annotated as significantly downregulated in the volcano plot, and Figure 2H shows GO:BP enrichment analysis confirming inflammatory pathways.

claim: Male AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia showed downregulation of GO:BP terms such as 'cellular response to lipopolysaccharide', 'inflammatory response', and 'NF-kappaB signaling'.
source: In contrast to females, downregulated genes in males were dominated by classical proinflammatory mediators such as Il1b, Il1a, Tnf, and Cxcl2 and enrichment analyses revealed downregulation of GO:BP terms such as 'cellular response to lipopolysaccharide', inflammatory response', and 'NF-kappaB signaling' (Figure 2H).
evidence: Figure 2H shows GO:BP enrichment analysis results listing these inflammatory terms as significantly enriched in downregulated genes from male Cst7-/- microglia.

claim: There was very little overlap between Cst7-regulated genes in males and females with only two genes shared including Cst7.
source: There was very little overlap between Cst7-regulated genes in males and females with only two genes shared including Cst7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 2C shows a Venn diagram demonstrating minimal overlap (2 genes) between DEGs in male vs. female Cst7-/- microglia.

claim: In AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ microglia, there were 33 DEGs between male vs. female.
source: In AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ microglia, there were 33 DEGs between male vs. female approximately evenly split between transcripts enriched in males vs. those enriched in females, whereas in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- we observed 240 DEGs dominated by those enriched in females (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 2D shows bar graphs quantifying DEGs between males and females in both AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- groups.

claim: In AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia, there were 240 DEGs between male vs. female, dominated by those enriched in females.
source: In AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ microglia, there were 33 DEGs between male vs. female approximately evenly split between transcripts enriched in males vs. those enriched in females, whereas in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- we observed 240 DEGs dominated by those enriched in females (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 2D shows bar graphs quantifying DEGs between males and females, with the AppNL-G-FCst7-/- group showing 240 DEGs predominantly enriched in females.

claim: Lilrb4a expression in IBA1+ cells was increased in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- vs. AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ in females but not in males.
source: We confirmed expression of Lilrb4a in microglia specifically around plaques and validated our RNASeq data showing an identical expression pattern to that observed previously with increased expression of microglial Lilrb4a in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- vs. AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ in females but not in males (Figure 2—figure supplement 3E and F).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 2F shows quantification of Lilrb4a expression in IBA1+ cells demonstrating increased expression in female Cst7-/- mice but not in males, validating the RNASeq findings.

claim: AppNL-G-F knock-in led to marked build-up of 6E10+ Aβ plaques in both males and females.
source: As expected, knock-in of the AppNL-G-F construct led to marked build-up of 6E10+ Aβ plaques, an increase in IBA1+ microglial burden around these plaques, and upregulation of LAMP2 in microglia predominantly in plaque-associated microglia in both males and females (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows immunofluorescence images demonstrating 6E10+ plaques in AppNL-G-F brains but not in wild-type brains in both sexes.

claim: AppNL-G-F knock-in led to an increase in IBA1+ microglial burden around plaques in both males and females.
source: As expected, knock-in of the AppNL-G-F construct led to marked build-up of 6E10+ Aβ plaques, an increase in IBA1+ microglial burden around these plaques, and upregulation of LAMP2 in microglia predominantly in plaque-associated microglia in both males and females (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows increased IBA1 staining around plaques in AppNL-G-F brains, and Figure 3B-D quantify increased IBA1 coverage in disease brains.

claim: AppNL-G-F knock-in led to upregulation of LAMP2 in microglia predominantly in plaque-associated microglia in both males and females.
source: As expected, knock-in of the AppNL-G-F construct led to marked build-up of 6E10+ Aβ plaques, an increase in IBA1+ microglial burden around these plaques, and upregulation of LAMP2 in microglia predominantly in plaque-associated microglia in both males and females (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows increased LAMP2 staining in AppNL-G-F brains, particularly around plaques, and Figure 3F-H quantify increased LAMP2 burden in disease brains.

claim: There was a trend towards increased IBA1+ microglial burden in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- mice in all brain regions, statistically significant in the subiculum.
source: We observed a trend towards increased IBA1+ microglial burden in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- mice in all brain regions, statistically significant in the subiculum (Figure 3B–D), more evidently in male mice.
evidence: Figure 3B-D show quantification of IBA1 coverage in cortex, hippocampus, and subiculum, with significant increases in the subiculum for Cst7-/- mice.

claim: LAMP2 predominantly co-localized with IBA1, suggesting expression is predominant in mononuclear phagocytes.
source: LAMP2 predominantly co-localised with IBA1, suggesting that expression is predominant in mononuclear phagocytes rather than neuronal cells or macroglia.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by the immunofluorescence images in Figure 3A and 3E showing co-localization of LAMP2 with IBA1.

claim: Microglial-normalized LAMP2 staining in the subiculum was reduced in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- vs. AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ males but increased in females.
source: Strikingly, we found in the subiculum that microglial-normalised LAMP2 staining followed the same pattern as many of the genes identified by microglia RNASeq with reduced expression in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- vs. AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ males but increased expression in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- vs. AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ females (Figure 3E, quantification in Figure 3H).
evidence: Figure 3H shows quantification of IBA1/LAMP2 ratio in the subiculum demonstrating decreased values in male Cst7-/- mice and increased values in female Cst7-/- mice.

claim: Aβ plaques had a far greater MeX04:6E10 ratio in the subiculum compared to other brain regions.
source: We found that Aβ plaques had a far greater MeX04:6E10 ratio in the subiculum compared to other brain regions (Figure 3I and J, quantified in Figure 3K), most likely caused by earlier Aβ accumulation in this region (Rönnbäck et al., 2011; Gail Canter et al., 2019) that may be dependent on a subpopulation of microglia (Spangenberg et al., 2019).
evidence: Figure 3K shows quantification of MeX04:6E10 ratio across brain regions, with the subiculum showing significantly higher ratios than cortex and hippocampus.

claim: Female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia had a greater percentage of MeX04+ microglia compared to AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ counterparts.
source: Consistent with our RNASeq and histology data suggesting increased lysosomal capacity specifically in female AppNL-G-F mice following deletion of Cst7, we observed a greater Aβ burden in female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia compared to AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ counterparts measured by both % Aβ-positive microglia (Figure 4B) and mean fluorescence intensity of MeX04 on microglia (Figure 4C).
evidence: Figure 4B shows quantification of percentage MeX04+ microglia, demonstrating significantly higher percentages in female Cst7-/- mice compared to controls.

claim: Female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia had greater mean fluorescence intensity of MeX04 compared to AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ counterparts.
source: Consistent with our RNASeq and histology data suggesting increased lysosomal capacity specifically in female AppNL-G-F mice following deletion of Cst7, we observed a greater Aβ burden in female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia compared to AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ counterparts measured by both % Aβ-positive microglia (Figure 4B) and mean fluorescence intensity of MeX04 on microglia (Figure 4C).
evidence: Figure 4C shows quantification of MeX04 median fluorescence intensity on microglia, demonstrating significantly higher intensity in female Cst7-/- mice compared to controls.

claim: There was no difference in microglial Aβ burden between male AppNL-G-FCst7-/- and AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ mice.
source: Interestingly, despite a reduced expression of lysosomal membrane marker LAMP2 in male AppNL-G-FCst7-/- mice compared to AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ counterparts (Figure 3C and D), we observed no difference in microglial Aβ burden (Figure 4B).
evidence: Figure 4B shows no significant difference in percentage MeX04+ microglia between male Cst7-/- and control mice.

claim: AppNL-G-F microglia had increased expression of CD45, CD11c, and MHCII compared to wild-type counterparts.
source: AppNL-G-F microglia had increased expression of CD45, CD11c, and MHCII compared to wild-type counterparts (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: Figure 4D-F show flow cytometry quantification demonstrating significantly increased expression of these markers in AppNL-G-F microglia compared to wild-type.

claim: Cst7 deletion did not lead to any significant differences in detection of CD45, CD11c, MHCII, or P2Y12 markers.
source: Cst7 deletion did not lead to any significant differences in detection of these markers, although we did note a trend towards increased MHCII+ microglia only in female mice, perhaps consistent with elevated endolysosomal activity and our RNASeq data suggesting an increase in antigen presentation pathway genes specifically in this group.
evidence: Figure 4D-G show no significant differences between Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- groups for these markers, though there is a trend for MHCII in females.

claim: Microglia isolated from 12-month AppNL-G-F mice cultured for 3 days express 20-fold more Cst7 than age-matched wild-type counterparts.
source: We found that microglia isolated from AppNL-G-F mice then cultured for 3 days express 20-fold more Cst7 than from age-matched wild-type counterparts (Figure 5B).
evidence: Figure 5B shows qPCR data demonstrating significantly higher Cst7 expression in cultured AppNL-G-F microglia compared to wild-type.

claim: Microglia isolated from 12-month AppNL-G-F mice cultured for 3 days express two-fold less Tmem119 than wild-type counterparts.
source: We also found that these AppNL-G-F microglia express two-fold less Tmem119, an established microglial homeostatic gene, than wild-type cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: Figure 5C shows qPCR data demonstrating significantly lower Tmem119 expression in cultured AppNL-G-F microglia compared to wild-type.

claim: Cst7 deletion does not affect degradation of Aβ1-42 in cultured microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: We used a pulse-chase live-imaging assay and found that Cst7 deletion does not affect degradation of Aβ1-42 (Figure 5—figure supplement 4E), a process dependent on cathepsins as it was inhibited by broad-spectrum inhibitors K777 and Ca074-Me (Figure 5—figure supplement 4F).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 4E shows no significant difference in Aβ degradation curves between AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia.

claim: Cst7 deletion does not affect intracellular activity of cathepsins L and C in cultured microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: We also showed that Cst7 deletion does not affect intracellular activity of cathepsins L and C (Figure 5D and E), targets of cystatin-F (Hamilton et al., 2008), or microglial lysosomal hydrolysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 4G).
evidence: Figure 5D and 5E show no significant differences in cathepsin L and C activity between AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia.

claim: Cst7 deletion does not affect microglial lysosomal hydrolysis in cultured microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: We also showed that Cst7 deletion does not affect intracellular activity of cathepsins L and C (Figure 5D and E), targets of cystatin-F (Hamilton et al., 2008), or microglial lysosomal hydrolysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 4G).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 4G shows no significant difference in DQ-BSA de-quenching (lysosomal hydrolysis) between AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia.

claim: Cst7 deletion led to a significant increase in microglial phagocytosis of myelin debris in cultured microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: We found that Cst7 deletion led to a significant increase in microglial phagocytosis of myelin debris (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: Figure 5F shows time-lapse images of myelin uptake, and Figure 5G shows quantification demonstrating significantly increased uptake in AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia compared to controls.

claim: In males, there was no effect of Cst7 genotype on plaque burden in any brain region.
source: In males, there was no effect of Cst7 genotype on plaque burden in any region (Figure 6B–F).
evidence: Figure 6B-F show quantification of Aβ plaque burden across multiple brain regions with no significant differences between male Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- mice.

claim: Despite increased lysosomal burden and intramicroglial Aβ load in female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- mice, there was no decrease in amyloid plaque burden in any region.
source: Surprisingly, despite an increased lysosomal burden (Figure 3F) and intramicroglial Aβ load (Figure 4B) in female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- mice, there was no decrease in amyloid plaque burden in any region.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Figure 6B-F showing no significant decreases in plaque burden in female Cst7-/- mice across brain regions.

claim: There was a significant increase in plaque number in the subiculum of female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- mice compared to controls.
source: In order to further probe the increase in amyloid pathology in the subiculum, we used MeX04 labelling of the dense cores of Aβ plaques and counted the number of plaques in this region. We observed a significant although modest increase in plaque number specifically in the females (Figure 6G, quantification in Figure 6H) without any difference in average plaque size detected (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 6H shows quantification of MeX04+ plaque count in the subiculum, demonstrating significantly higher counts in female Cst7-/- mice compared to controls.

claim: There was no difference in average plaque size in the subiculum between female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- and control mice.
source: We observed a significant although modest increase in plaque number specifically in the females (Figure 6G, quantification in Figure 6H) without any difference in average plaque size detected (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 6—figure supplement 1A shows no significant difference in MeX04+ plaque area between female Cst7-/- and control mice.

claim: There was loss of synaptophysin coverage around plaques in AppNL-G-F brains.
source: We observed loss of Sy38 coverage around plaques (Figure 6I) and a small but significant decrease in coverage between AppNL-G-F/Cst7-/- vs. AppNL-G-F brains only in females (Figure 6J).
evidence: Figure 6I shows immunofluorescence images demonstrating reduced synaptophysin staining around plaques, and Figure 6J quantifies this reduction.

claim: There was a small but significant decrease in synaptophysin coverage in female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- brains compared to AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ brains.
source: We observed loss of Sy38 coverage around plaques (Figure 6I) and a small but significant decrease in coverage between AppNL-G-F/Cst7-/- vs. AppNL-G-F brains only in females (Figure 6J).
evidence: Figure 6J shows quantification of synaptophysin coverage demonstrating a significant decrease in female Cst7-/- mice compared to controls.

claim: Microglia play numerous roles in development and homeostasis.
source: Microglia are the predominant immune cells of the brain parenchyma and play numerous roles in development and homeostasis (Colonna and Butovsky, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a published review article.

claim: Single nucleotide polymorphisms leading to altered risk for late-onset AD are enriched in microglial-expressed genes associated with endolysosomal function and lipid handling.
source: In recent years, microglia have become heavily implicated in the pathogenesis of AD, in part due to accumulating genetic and epigenetic evidence that single nucleotide polymorphisms leading to altered risk for late-onset AD (LOAD) are enriched in microglial-expressed genes associated with endolysosomal function and lipid handling (Podleśny-Drabiniok et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a published study.

claim: Women are up to twice as likely to be diagnosed with AD than men.
source: In addition to genetics, sex is a major risk factor for AD, with women up to twice as likely to be diagnosed than men (Podcasy and Epperson, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a published study.

claim: The increased risk of AD in women is not entirely due to increased longevity in females.
source: This sex bias is not entirely due to increased longevity in females, as increased risk remains after adjusting for lifespan, and may be due to interaction effects between sex/gender and genetics (Gamache et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a published study.

claim: Disease-associated microglia (DAM/MGnD/ARM) are characterized by downregulation of microglial homeostatic genes Tmem119 and P2ry12 and upregulation of genes such as Apoe, Spp1, Itgax, Clec7a, and Cst7.
source: Recently, an altered state of microglia has been identified in AD models that arises dependent on AD risk gene TREM2. These cells, termed disease-associated microglia (DAM)/microglial neurodegenerative phenotype (MGnD)/activated response microglia (ARM) (Keren-Shaul et al., 2017; Krasemann et al., 2017; Sala Frigerio et al., 2019), are characterised by downregulation of microglial 'homeostatic' genes Tmem119 and P2ry12 and upregulation of genes such as Apoe, Spp1, Itgax, Clec7a, and Cst7.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to the original papers describing these microglial states.

claim: The emergence of the DAM/MGnD/ARM subset may be accelerated in female mice compared to male.
source: Notably, the emergence of this subset may be accelerated in female mice compared to male (Sala Frigerio et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a published study.

claim: DAM/MGnD/ARM are believed to be highly phagocytic cells due to the enrichment of phagocytic and lipid-handling pathways in their gene sets.
source: DAM/MGnD/ARM are believed to be highly phagocytic cells due to the enrichment of phagocytic and lipid-handling pathways in their gene sets (Deczkowska et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a published review.

claim: Cst7/CF expression appears to be driven by amyloid plaques as upregulation at both the RNA and protein level is spatially localized to plaques.
source: Cst7/CF expression appears to be driven by amyloid plaques as upregulation at both the RNA and protein level is spatially localised to plaques (Ofengeim et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to published studies, and is further validated by the in situ hybridization data in Figure 1.

claim: CF is atypical in that it is localized to the endolysosomal compartment where it acts as an endogenous inhibitor of cysteine proteases such as cathepsin L and C.
source: CF is atypical in that it is localised to the endolysosomal compartment where it acts as an endogenous inhibitor of cysteine proteases such as cathepsin L and C (Hamilton et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a published study.

claim: Some studies have suggested CF may play a protective role in a demyelination model by inhibiting cathepsin C.
source: Some studies have suggested CF may play a protective role in a demyelination model by inhibiting cathepsin C (Liang et al., 2016) or negatively regulating microglial phagocytosis (Kang et al., 2018; Popescu et al., 2023) but the possible disease-modifying role of Cst7/CF in amyloid-driven neurodegenerative disease is unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to published studies.

claim: Some studies have suggested CF may negatively regulate microglial phagocytosis.
source: Some studies have suggested CF may play a protective role in a demyelination model by inhibiting cathepsin C (Liang et al., 2016) or negatively regulating microglial phagocytosis (Kang et al., 2018; Popescu et al., 2023) but the possible disease-modifying role of Cst7/CF in amyloid-driven neurodegenerative disease is unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to published studies.

claim: There is some evidence that Cst7 itself is upregulated to a greater extent in female vs. male mice.
source: Additionally, although there is some evidence that Cst7 itself is upregulated to a greater extent in female vs. male mice (Kang et al., 2018; Sala Frigerio et al., 2019; Guillot-Sestier et al., 2021), the sex-specific role of Cst7 in disease has not been investigated.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to published studies, and is supported by data in Figure 1A.

claim: Cst7 negatively regulates phagocytosis in microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: Together, these data suggest that, in females, Cst7/CF negatively regulates phagocytosis but does not affect lysosomal proteolysis or PRR-driven inflammatory cytokine production in microglia from the AppNL-G-F model of amyloid-driven AD.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the in vitro phagocytosis assays shown in Figure 5F-G demonstrating increased phagocytosis in Cst7-/- microglia, combined with the lack of effect on degradation and cathepsin activity.

claim: Cst7 does not affect lysosomal proteolysis in microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: Together, these data suggest that, in females, Cst7/CF negatively regulates phagocytosis but does not affect lysosomal proteolysis or PRR-driven inflammatory cytokine production in microglia from the AppNL-G-F model of amyloid-driven AD.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the degradation assays and cathepsin activity assays shown in Figure 5D-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 4E-G showing no differences between Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia.

claim: Cst7 does not affect PRR-driven inflammatory cytokine production in microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: Together, these data suggest that, in females, Cst7/CF negatively regulates phagocytosis but does not affect lysosomal proteolysis or PRR-driven inflammatory cytokine production in microglia from the AppNL-G-F model of amyloid-driven AD.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the cytokine secretion assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4B-D showing no differences in IL-6, IL-1β, or TNFα secretion between Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia.

claim: Cst7/CF is upregulated along with numerous cathepsin genes in order to prevent potentially harmful protease activity.
source: Perhaps counterintuitively, Cst7 (a reported cysteine protease inhibitor) is robustly upregulated in microglia alongside concomitant upregulation of cysteine proteases such as cathepsins D, B, L, and Z. In fact, such internal regulation systems are not uncommon in inflammation biology, where proinflammatory mediators such as IL-1β and IL-18 are negatively regulated by co-expressed IL-1 receptor antagonist and IL-18 binding protein, respectively (Hurme and Santtila, 1998; Dinarello et al., 2013). We therefore hypothesise that Cst7/CF is upregulated along with numerous cathepsin genes in order to prevent potentially harmful protease activity (Turk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the discussion, supported by citations to literature on similar regulatory systems and harmful protease activity.

claim: CF deficiency may lead to an increase in secreted cathepsin activity, which promotes phagocytosis.
source: It is possible that CF deficiency does in fact lead to an increase in cathepsin activity, but CF itself is secreted and only impairs secreted cathepsins which are responsible for promoting phagocytosis. Indeed, studies have suggested that CF can be secreted and that there is a role for secreted cathepsins in phagocytosis (Liuzzo et al., 1999; Hamilton et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation stated in the discussion, supported by citations to studies on CF secretion and cathepsin roles in phagocytosis.

claim: Male microglia are believed to have higher baseline activity in processes such as inflammation, antigen presentation, and phagocytosis.
source: In general, male microglia are believed to have higher baseline activity in processes such as inflammation, antigen presentation, and phagocytosis; whereas female microglia are more associated with neuroprotection and the DAM/ARM/MGnD signature in ageing and disease (Guneykaya et al., 2018; Kodama and Gan, 2019; Sala Frigerio et al., 2019; Villa et al., 2019; Guillot-Sestier et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to multiple published studies on sex differences in microglia.

claim: Female microglia are more associated with neuroprotection and the DAM/ARM/MGnD signature in ageing and disease.
source: In general, male microglia are believed to have higher baseline activity in processes such as inflammation, antigen presentation, and phagocytosis; whereas female microglia are more associated with neuroprotection and the DAM/ARM/MGnD signature in ageing and disease (Guneykaya et al., 2018; Kodama and Gan, 2019; Sala Frigerio et al., 2019; Villa et al., 2019; Guillot-Sestier et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to multiple published studies on sex differences in microglia.

claim: Sexual dimorphism of microglia in adults appears to be a cell-intrinsic phenomenon.
source: Indeed, sexual dimorphism of microglia in adults appears a cell-intrinsic phenomenon as female microglia transplanted in male brains retain their transcriptional profile and reduce infarct size in males after ischemic stroke (Villa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to a published transplantation study.

claim: Deletion of Cst3 (cystatin C) led to protection in the EAE model of multiple sclerosis in females but not males.
source: This sex-dependent interaction effect has previously been observed in studies investigating the cystatin/cathepsin system, where deletion of Cst3 (cystatin C) led to protection in the EAE model of multiple sclerosis in females but not males (Hoghooghi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to a published study.

claim: The presence of the APOE E4 allele confers a greater AD risk in women than in men.
source: One example of this interaction is APOE, in which the presence of the E4 allele confers a greater AD risk in women than in men (Altmann et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to a published study.

claim: Microglia lacking TAM receptors Axl and Mer fail to take up Aβ which leads to an overall decrease in dense-core plaque formation.
source: For example, microglia lacking TAM receptors Axl and Mer fail to take up Aβ which leads to an overall decrease in dense-core plaque formation (Huang et al., 2021), microglia can 'seed' plaques from disease tissue into engrafted, non-affected regions (d'Errico et al., 2022), and either genetic or pharmacological depletion of microglia leads to a reduction in plaque burden/intensity accompanied by increase in cerebral amyloid angiopathy (Spangenberg et al., 2019; Kiani Shabestari et al., 2022) perhaps through redistributing Aβ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to a published study.

claim: Microglia can seed plaques from disease tissue into engrafted, non-affected regions.
source: For example, microglia lacking TAM receptors Axl and Mer fail to take up Aβ which leads to an overall decrease in dense-core plaque formation (Huang et al., 2021), microglia can 'seed' plaques from disease tissue into engrafted, non-affected regions (d'Errico et al., 2022), and either genetic or pharmacological depletion of microglia leads to a reduction in plaque burden/intensity accompanied by increase in cerebral amyloid angiopathy (Spangenberg et al., 2019; Kiani Shabestari et al., 2022) perhaps through redistributing Aβ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation to a published study.

claim: Genetic or pharmacological depletion of microglia leads to a reduction in plaque burden/intensity accompanied by increase in cerebral amyloid angiopathy.
source: For example, microglia lacking TAM receptors Axl and Mer fail to take up Aβ which leads to an overall decrease in dense-core plaque formation (Huang et al., 2021), microglia can 'seed' plaques from disease tissue into engrafted, non-affected regions (d'Errico et al., 2022), and either genetic or pharmacological depletion of microglia leads to a reduction in plaque burden/intensity accompanied by increase in cerebral amyloid angiopathy (Spangenberg et al., 2019; Kiani Shabestari et al., 2022) perhaps through redistributing Aβ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to published studies.

claim: Cst7/CF may contribute to restraining plaque formation and protecting against synapse loss by influencing microglial endolysosomal function in a dose-dependent manner.
source: We speculate that Cst7/CF may contribute to restraining plaque formation and protecting against synapse loss by influencing microglial endolysosomal function in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion stated in the discussion based on the findings that Cst7 deletion leads to increased phagocytosis, increased plaque burden, and increased synapse loss in females.

claim: CST7 protein levels predicted slower tau accumulation and cognitive decline with a significant sex interaction effect in humans.
source: CST7 protein has also been detected as higher levels predicted slower tau accumulation and cognitive decline with a significant sex interaction effect (Pereira et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the limitations section with a citation to a published human study.

claim: Overexpression of TREM2 in human microglial cells driving CST7 expression led to inhibition of phagocytosis in a CST7-dependent manner.
source: Indeed, a recent study utilised overexpression of TREM2 in human microglial cells to show that driving CST7 expression led to inhibition of phagocytosis in a CST7-dependent manner (Popescu et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the limitations section with a citation to a recent published study.

claim: Cst7 was the most differentially expressed gene in both sexes when comparing AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- groups.
source: Importantly, Cst7 itself was the most DEG in both sexes, confirming successful deletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 2A shows Cst7 expression data confirming it was the most significantly downregulated gene in Cst7-/- mice, validating the knockout.

claim: Intraperitoneal injection of MeX04 2.5 hr before microglial isolation by FACS can detect Aβ-containing microglia.
source: First, we validated that intraperitoneal injection of MeX04 2.5 hr before microglial isolation by FACS can detect Aβ-containing microglia. Wild-type and AppNL-G-F mice were aged to 12 months and injected with either MeX04 or vehicle before microglial isolation by FACS as previously but with additional detection of MeX04 in the DAPI channel. As expected, wild-type+MeX04 and AppNL-G-F+vehicle mice displayed a background MeX04 signal that was shifted only in the AppNL-G-F+MeX04 group (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 4—figure supplement 1 shows FACS plots demonstrating MeX04+ microglia only in AppNL-G-F mice injected with MeX04, validating the approach.

claim: Cst7 deletion had no effect on isolation yield of microglia from AppNL-G-F mice.
source: We then used this validated system to compare functional properties of microglia isolated from female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- and AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ mice. First, we showed that Cst7 knockout had no effect on isolation yield (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A) and observed no differences in inflammatory cytokine secretion in response to LPS or NLRP3 activation stimulus silica (Figure 5—figure supplement 4B–D), as predicted from our previous RNASeq analysis in female mice.
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 4A shows no significant difference in CD11b+ cell yield between AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- mice.

claim: Cst7 deletion had no effect on inflammatory cytokine secretion in response to LPS or NLRP3 activation in cultured microglia from female AppNL-G-F mice.
source: We then used this validated system to compare functional properties of microglia isolated from female AppNL-G-FCst7-/- and AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ mice. First, we showed that Cst7 knockout had no effect on isolation yield (Figure 5—figure supplement 4A) and observed no differences in inflammatory cytokine secretion in response to LPS or NLRP3 activation stimulus silica (Figure 5—figure supplement 4B–D), as predicted from our previous RNASeq analysis in female mice.
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 4B-D show no significant differences in IL-6, IL-1β, or TNFα secretion between AppNL-G-FCst7+/+ and AppNL-G-FCst7-/- microglia in response to LPS or LPS+silica.

claim: Degradation of Aβ1-42 is dependent on cathepsins as it was inhibited by broad-spectrum inhibitors K777 and Ca074-Me.
source: We used a pulse-chase live-imaging assay and found that Cst7 deletion does not affect degradation of Aβ1-42 (Figure 5—figure supplement 4E), a process dependent on cathepsins as it was inhibited by broad-spectrum inhibitors K777 and Ca074-Me (Figure 5—figure supplement 4F).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 4F shows that cathepsin inhibitors K777 and Ca074-Me significantly inhibit Aβ degradation, demonstrating cathepsin dependence.

claim: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia from young adult non-diseased mice, there was no significant difference in uptake of Aβ oligomers, human AD synaptoneurosomes, Staphylococcus aureus bioparticles, or myelin debris.
source: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia, we observed no significant difference in uptake of Aβ oligomers, human AD synaptoneurosomes, Staphylococcus aureus bioparticles, or myelin debris (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D); degradation of Aβ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E); or lysosomal hydrolysis measured by the ability to cleave the quencher molecule from DQ-BSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F); transcriptional response to LPS, IL-4, or apoptotic neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–I); cytokine secretion in response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) or NLRP3 inflammasome activation by silica particles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J and K).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-D show no significant differences in uptake of various substrates between wild-type and Cst7-/- microglia from non-diseased mice.

claim: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia from young adult non-diseased mice, there was no significant difference in degradation of Aβ.
source: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia, we observed no significant difference in uptake of Aβ oligomers, human AD synaptoneurosomes, Staphylococcus aureus bioparticles, or myelin debris (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D); degradation of Aβ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E); or lysosomal hydrolysis measured by the ability to cleave the quencher molecule from DQ-BSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F); transcriptional response to LPS, IL-4, or apoptotic neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–I); cytokine secretion in response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) or NLRP3 inflammasome activation by silica particles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J and K).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1E shows no significant difference in Aβ degradation between wild-type and Cst7-/- microglia from non-diseased mice.

claim: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia from young adult non-diseased mice, there was no significant difference in lysosomal hydrolysis measured by DQ-BSA cleavage.
source: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia, we observed no significant difference in uptake of Aβ oligomers, human AD synaptoneurosomes, Staphylococcus aureus bioparticles, or myelin debris (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D); degradation of Aβ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E); or lysosomal hydrolysis measured by the ability to cleave the quencher molecule from DQ-BSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F); transcriptional response to LPS, IL-4, or apoptotic neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–I); cytokine secretion in response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) or NLRP3 inflammasome activation by silica particles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J and K).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1F shows no significant difference in DQ-BSA de-quenching between wild-type and Cst7-/- microglia from non-diseased mice.

claim: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia from young adult non-diseased mice, there was no significant difference in transcriptional response to LPS, IL-4, or apoptotic neurons.
source: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia, we observed no significant difference in uptake of Aβ oligomers, human AD synaptoneurosomes, Staphylococcus aureus bioparticles, or myelin debris (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D); degradation of Aβ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E); or lysosomal hydrolysis measured by the ability to cleave the quencher molecule from DQ-BSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F); transcriptional response to LPS, IL-4, or apoptotic neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–I); cytokine secretion in response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) or NLRP3 inflammasome activation by silica particles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J and K).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1G-I show no significant differences in gene expression (Arg1, Il1b, Trem2) in response to various stimuli between wild-type and Cst7-/- microglia from non-diseased mice.

claim: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia from young adult non-diseased mice, there was no significant difference in cytokine secretion in response to LPS or IL-4.
source: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia, we observed no significant difference in uptake of Aβ oligomers, human AD synaptoneurosomes, Staphylococcus aureus bioparticles, or myelin debris (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D); degradation of Aβ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E); or lysosomal hydrolysis measured by the ability to cleave the quencher molecule from DQ-BSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F); transcriptional response to LPS, IL-4, or apoptotic neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–I); cytokine secretion in response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) or NLRP3 inflammasome activation by silica particles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J and K).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 2 shows no significant differences in multiple cytokine secretion levels between wild-type and Cst7-/- microglia from non-diseased mice in response to LPS or IL-4.

claim: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia from young adult non-diseased mice, there was no significant difference in NLRP3 inflammasome activation by silica particles.
source: Comparing Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia, we observed no significant difference in uptake of Aβ oligomers, human AD synaptoneurosomes, Staphylococcus aureus bioparticles, or myelin debris (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D); degradation of Aβ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E); or lysosomal hydrolysis measured by the ability to cleave the quencher molecule from DQ-BSA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F); transcriptional response to LPS, IL-4, or apoptotic neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–I); cytokine secretion in response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) or NLRP3 inflammasome activation by silica particles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J and K).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1J and K show no significant differences in IL-1β secretion in response to LPS+silica between wild-type and Cst7-/- microglia from non-diseased mice.

claim: siRNA knockdown of Cst7 in BV-2 cells achieved 70% reduction in gene expression.
source: We also addressed the possibility of compensation in adult knockout mice by using siRNA to knock down Cst7 in the BV-2 microglia cell line and found that, despite 70% reduction in gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A), Cst7 knockdown had no effect on IL-6 secretion (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B) or transcriptional changes response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C–E).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 3A shows qPCR data demonstrating approximately 70% reduction in Cst7 expression in siRNA-treated BV-2 cells.

claim: Cst7 knockdown in BV-2 cells had no effect on IL-6 secretion or transcriptional changes in response to LPS or IL-4.
source: We also addressed the possibility of compensation in adult knockout mice by using siRNA to knock down Cst7 in the BV-2 microglia cell line and found that, despite 70% reduction in gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A), Cst7 knockdown had no effect on IL-6 secretion (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B) or transcriptional changes response to LPS or IL-4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C–E).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 3B-E show no significant differences in IL-6 secretion or gene expression (Arg1, Il1b, Trem2) between scrambled control and Cst7 knockdown BV-2 cells.

claim: The increased plaque burden in female Cst7-/- mice may lead to increased synapse loss.
source: This reflects the effect observed with plaque coverage above suggesting the increased plaque burden in Cst7-/- female mice may lead to increased synapse loss.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the synaptophysin coverage data in Figure 6J showing reduced coverage in female Cst7-/- mice.

claim: The sex-dependent effects of Cst7 deletion on microglial lysosomes may be driven by plaque composition/structure.
source: This implies that the sex-dependent effects of Cst7 deletion on microglial lysosomes may be driven by plaque composition/structure, with regions dominated by dense core plaques (indicating further 'disease progression') showing greater effect of Cst7 deletion.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the MeX04:6E10 ratio data in Figure 3K and the LAMP2 data in Figure 3H showing region-dependent effects.

claim: Regions dominated by dense core plaques show greater effect of Cst7 deletion on microglial lysosomes.
source: This implies that the sex-dependent effects of Cst7 deletion on microglial lysosomes may be driven by plaque composition/structure, with regions dominated by dense core plaques (indicating further 'disease progression') showing greater effect of Cst7 deletion.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation connecting the higher MeX04:6E10 ratio in subiculum (Figure 3K) with the stronger sex-dependent LAMP2 effects in that region (Figure 3H).

claim: Microglia isolated from 12-month-old AppNL-G-F mice cultured for 3 days retain key elements of their in vivo disease transcriptional identity.
source: These data suggest that, despite removal from a disease brain and subsequent culture in vitro, 12-month-old AppNL-G-F microglia retain key elements of their in vivo disease transcriptional identity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the qPCR data in Figure 5B and 5C showing that cultured AppNL-G-F microglia maintain high Cst7 and low Tmem119 expression.

claim: The increased microglial Aβ burden in female Cst7-/- mice in vivo is due to increased uptake rather than impaired degradation.
source: However, in vivo it is challenging to ascertain whether the increase in microglial Aβ is due to an increased uptake or to an impaired degradation. To test this, we conducted in vitro assays on Cst7+/+ and Cst7-/- microglia to examine phagolysosomal and related functions.
evidence: This is implied by the combination of findings: increased microglial Aβ in vivo (Figure 4B-C), no effect on degradation or cathepsin activity (Figure 5D-E, Figure 5—figure supplement 4E-G), and increased phagocytosis (Figure 5F-G).

claim: Cst7 is expressed at very low levels basally in non-diseased microglia.
source: Unlike constitutively highly expressed microglial genes such as Trem2 where knockout leads to dramatic alterations in in vitro phenotype (Takahashi et al., 2005; Hsieh et al., 2009; Kleinberger et al., 2014; Yeh et al., 2016), Cst7 is expressed at very low levels basally (Sala Frigerio et al., 2019; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and reference to Figure 1A showing low baseline Cst7 expression in wild-type mice.

claim: Cst7 deletion would have limited impact on microglial phenotype at baseline where Cst7 is not highly expressed.
source: Therefore, we reasoned that Cst7 deletion would have limited impact on microglial phenotype at baseline where Cst7 is not highly expressed.
evidence: This is stated as reasoning for why baseline functional assays in non-diseased Cst7-/- microglia showed no differences (Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and 2).
